front.title: Signaling RSVP-TE Tunnels on an SRv6 Forwarding Plane Using End.X Segment Identifiers

abstract.t:
RFC 8577 defines mechanisms to signal RSVP-TE tunnels on a shared MPLS forwarding plane by introducing the notion of per-TE link labels that are functionally equivalent to SR-MPLS adjacency segments. This document extends that work to the SRv6 data plane, defining the signaling extensions and procedures necessary to establish RSVP-TE tunnels that utilize SRv6 Segment Identifiers (SIDs) for forwarding.
This document specifies how SRv6 End.X SIDs that are advertised in the IGP serve as TE link SIDs, defines new RSVP signaling extensions for carrying SRv6 SIDs and for influencing the endpoint behavior flavors of the SIDs, describes TE path segment-list construction procedures at the ingress (including NEXT-CSID compressed segment lists), adapts the delegation mechanisms of RFC 8577 to use SRv6 Binding SIDs, and describes the termination of the tunnel at the egress. The result couples the traffic engineering capabilities of the RSVP-TE control plane with the native IPv6 forwarding of SRv6.
